Strategy is staged from cheap/structural to expensive/semantic: (1) pre-flight evidence checks against the cited finding IDs and source_policy blocks; (2) structural shell-grep tests that exactly mirror the operator-provided test_plan; (3) semantic reviewer checks that the test_plan shell tests CANNOT catch (charter phrase provenance, citation accuracy, drift-pattern chronology, branch-base correctness); (4) regression risks; (5) a binary accept/reject gate.
Each command in required_commands is paired with the expected output pattern so a future implementer can run it and compare verbatim. No test relies on the implementer's paraphrase of output.

Where the proposal contains a factual error (charter-citation drift, cycle-file vs finding-file confusion, default-branch confusion, dirty working tree), the manual_review_checks flag it explicitly so the implementer must reconcile before accepting the proposal as-is.

REGEX-INTERPRETATION: The operator-provided test_plan step 4 uses regex 'admin.dashboard|AI.workflow.platform'. In basic and extended grep, '.' matches ANY single character including space, so 'admin dashboard' (with space) DOES match 'admin.dashboard'. This is counterintuitive but verified experimentally: printf 'admin dashboard\n' | grep -E 'admin.dashboard' returns the line. The proposal's parenthetical explanation ('both will match if either phrase appears') is correct. NO ACTION REQUIRED but the implementer must understand why before adjusting the test_plan.

POLICY-COMPLETENESS: The proposal says 'there is no negative term for admin dashboard, AI workflow platform, or dashboard template'. Verified: source_policy.negative_terms is exactly ['gauge theory', 'refugee camp', 'OpenSCAD'] — confirmed no dashboard/workflow negative terms exist. The review doc's 'Queries to Retire' section should name specific negative-term additions (e.g., 'admin dashboard', 'AI workflow platform', 'dashboard template') so the diagnosis is actionable.

BOOST-TERM-UNBOUNDED: The proposal claims 'Next.js is a boost term that fires on every admin-dashboard template hit, drowning out the four guardian/lesson/curriculum/safety boosts'. Verified: boost_terms = ['Guardian', 'lesson', 'inference', 'Next.js', 'TypeScript', 'curriculum', 'safety'] — 7 boost terms. The review doc should not mis-count; the proposal text says 'four guardian/lesson/curriculum/safety boosts' but that's only 4 of the 7 boost terms ('inference' and 'TypeScript' are also boosts and would also fire on dashboard hits). If the implementer copies this count from the proposal, the review doc will understate the structural problem. The actual claim should be: 'Next.js, TypeScript, and inference are all unbounded boosts that fire on every generic dashboard hit, drowning out the four narrower guardian/lesson/curriculum/safety boosts.'

regression_risks: BRANCH-BASE-CONTAMINATION: If the implementer cuts the new branch from current HEAD (codex/xo-readiness-remediation) instead of origin/master, the new branch will carry over the dirty .agents/daily-digest.md and .stats/pennyone.db modifications, plus the untracked docs/security/ and knowledge/ directories. Even if the implementer only commits the two new files, downstream PR diffs against master will show 'unrelated changes' and may fail dirty-root isolation checks. Risk: HIGH. Mitigation: explicit checkout of master before branching, or git checkout -b research/proposed-xo-source-plan-review origin/master.

DIRTY-WORKING-TREE-COMMIT-CONTAMINATION: Even after branching from master, if .agents/daily-digest.md and .stats/pennyone.db are still modified in the worktree, an accidental git add -A could capture them. The implementer must use git add docs/research/XO_SOURCE_PLAN_REVIEW.md docs/research/README.md explicitly, never git add -A or git add ..

FINDING-ID-FABRICATION: The proposal explicitly warns 'Do NOT invent finding IDs that are not in the ledger.' Risk: MEDIUM. The four cited IDs are all verified present, but a careless implementer adding additional 'Older cycles' rows could fabricate IDs. Mitigation: the per-finding-ID grep loop in required_commands will catch any ID not in the ledger.

CHARTER-CITATION-DRIFT: Per CITATION-ERROR-1 above, if the review doc says 'guardian console' is in XO_CHARTER.md when it is actually in XO_GUARDIAN_CONSOLE.md, downstream consumers (corvus-forge live-fire, future QA passes) will cite an incorrect source. Risk: MEDIUM. Mitigation: require each charter phrase in the review doc to be cited inline with the foundation filename.

TEST-PLAN-FALSE-POSITIVE: The operator test_plan step 4 regex 'admin.dashboard|AI.workflow.platform' will match if EITHER 'admin dashboard' or 'AI workflow platform' appears. So a doc that contains 'admin dashboard' but not 'AI workflow platform' passes step 4, even though the proposal explicitly requires BOTH phrases in 'Queries to Retire'. Risk: MEDIUM. The implementer should verify both phrases appear, not rely on the test_plan alone. (Manual-review fix: extend required_commands to grep for each phrase individually.)

POLICY-EDIT-MISSED: The proposal's diagnosis is correct, but the doc it produces only DESCRIBES the source_policy gap; it does not EDIT the source_policy. If the operator later expects the collector to stop emitting dashboard drift, they will be surprised. Risk: LOW for THIS proposal (which is docs-only), but the doc should make explicit that the policy edit is a follow-up.

URL-DRIFT: The proposal lists ui-mtverse/free-nextjs-admin-dashboard-template as one of the four finding URLs, but no verified finding contains that exact URL — it appears in older cycles if at all. If the review doc cites a URL that is not in any cited finding, the URL will appear as ungrounded. Risk: LOW. Mitigation: verify each URL against the actual findings.jsonl rows before committing.
NO-RUN-EVIDENCE: The proposal is docs-only, so there are no runtime regressions. Risk: NONE for runtime. Documentation drift remains the dominant risk class for this change.
BRANCH-NAMING: 'research/proposed-xo-source-plan-review' — verified branch names like 'research/' are not currently in use in the repo (no results for search of similar branches). No naming conflict.
accept_reject_gate: PASS-ALL-OF: (1) all six operator-provided test_plan commands succeed with the expected outputs from required_commands above; (2) per-finding-ID grep loop returns count >=1 for each of the four IDs and count ==0 for any ID not in the four; (3) boost_terms and negative_terms set-equality checks pass against the four cited findings; (4) the new branch is based on origin/master (git log --oneline master..HEAD is empty before the new commit); (5) the new branch's first commit touches exactly docs/research/XO_SOURCE_PLAN_REVIEW.md and docs/research/README.md with no other files modified or staged; (6) the review doc cites each charter phrase with its foundation filename, and 'guardian console' is sourced from XO_GUARDIAN_CONSOLE.md not XO_CHARTER.md; (7) both 'admin dashboard' AND 'AI workflow platform' appear literally in the doc (not just one of them via the regex); (8) 'agentic', 'symlink', 'supply chain', and 'CVE' all appear literally in the doc.

REJECT-IF-ANY-OF: (a) any of the four cited finding IDs is missing or fabricated; (b) boost_terms or negative_terms in any cited finding does not match the proposal's claim verbatim; (c) the new branch is based on a non-master ref; (d) the new branch's first commit modifies files outside docs/research/; (e) the review doc claims 'guardian console' is in XO_CHARTER.md (it's in XO_GUARDIAN_CONSOLE.md); (f) the CVE evidence is cited only from cycle files without also citing the project_updates finding IDs that carry the canonical evidence rows; (g) the review doc lists 'ui-mtverse/free-nextjs-admin-dashboard-template' as a finding URL without citing the cycle file it came from; (h) the review doc understates the boost-term count ('four boosts' when there are actually seven); (i) docs/research/ is not created as a new directory but the file is placed at a different path; (j) the branch is named anything other than research/proposed-xo-source-plan-review.

ESCALATE-TO-OPERATOR: (alpha) if the implementer resolves CITATION-ERROR-1 differently than my recommendation (e.g., by removing 'guardian console' entirely from the review) — the operator should approve the substitute. (beta) if the implementer chooses a different base branch than master — the operator should approve. (gamma) if the chronology list in 'Observed Mismatch' expands beyond the six dates the proposal cites to include 2026-05-24 as the actual start — operator should approve since the evidence supports the earlier start. (delta) if the implementer adds negative-term proposals to source_policy in the same PR (instead of docs-only) — operator should approve, since it would close the loop but expands scope.

FINAL-GATE: After implementation, re-run all 20 required_commands and capture real output (not paraphrases). The implementing agent must paste the captured output verbatim. If any command exits non-zero or produces output that diverges from the expected patterns above, the implementation FAILS the gate regardless of how reasonable the prose looks.
